description: The family includes municipal police-reported crime rates, a Canada/province Crime Severity Index for 1998–2014, and a customised Alberta family-violence table for 2008–2010. The custom table combines Uniform Crime Reporting and Homicide Survey information on child/youth assault victims, senior violent-crime victims, family violence and homicides. Its distribution is XLSX. These are reported policing workloads; reporting-detachment geography can differ from offence location. The severity-index source explicitly identifies police-resource planning as a use. Clinical outcomes or unreported prevalence are not inferred. The sources retain different measures, periods and geographies within a curator-defined policing-statistics family. The CUDC source records name the Open Government Licence - Alberta. Costs, present file access and numerical contents are unverified. Specific simulation uses remain unstated unless identified above. No workbook, document or linked data body was fetched. An additional Uniform Crime Reporting companion gives property-crime rates per 100,000 population for Canada and provinces in 1998–2014, with CSV and PDF descriptors. Its source explicitly identifies allocation of police resources and programme planning as uses. Property crime remains a distinct measure from severity indices and family-violence counts. A further annual Canada/province table reports violent-crime rates per 100,000 residents for 1998–2014. CSV and PDF descriptors identify two representations. Its source explicitly links Uniform Crime Reporting data to police-resource planning and allocation. Police-substantiated incidents are distinct from unreported events or the separate self-reported spousal-violence survey; no workload equivalence is inferred.
